Best thing I did to conserve power was to find out exactly how much power each item actually used. I bought a digital power consumption measuring unit for about $30 that records what the item plugged into it uses and calculates the minute by minute cost.

Even if you find you cant make much change to the amount of power used, at least you actually know where it is going.

Any chance to use timers to power off things during the night? There are nowadays digital timers with wifi so you can actually setup a schedule for when to power things on and off on your phone/tablet. I guess this is great for people who own homes.

You can get simple digital timers to power things on/off but I have never really found a good use for them. No good for fridges and such, TV and computers I can turn off myself when finished.

There is another product I would recommend for a computer or stereo with extras such as printers, external screens, external speakers etc. Can't think what it is called at present but it looks like a power board with 4 or 6 general outlets and one 'driver' outlet. When the computer, which is connected to the 'driver' outlet goes to sleep or is shut off, the power to the other outlets automatically switches off also. Everything powers back up again when the computer restarts.

Their numbers are wrong, the actual situation is far worse, at least for DVRs. I've measured DVRs from 3 cable companies (both Motorola and Scientific Atlanta boxes, 3 different models), and they ALL used at least 90W *even when "OFF" *

Part of this is because they intentionally avoid upgrading because boxes older than 2006 are exempt from CableCARD requirements in place to keep them playing fair with TiVo etc.
